tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive solve after placing largest
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Identify the largest disk that is not yet on its goal peg, clear any smaller disks that block it, move it to its goal peg, then recursively solve the remaining disks.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the current configuration has the largest misplaced disk and you need to place it correctly before handling smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a larger disk while a smaller disk remains on top of it, resulting in an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Standard recursive transfer of k disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a target peg, recursively move k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the kth disk to the target, then move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary onto the target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to relocate a contiguous stack of disks while preserving their order.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move the bottom disk of a stack without first moving the disks above it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable block
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The response must end with a syntactically correct Python‑style list of moves; the verifier extracts the last such list.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When formatting the answer, ensure the move list is the final content of the response.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Including explanatory text after the move list, causing the parser to miss the moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration before output
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Replay each move mentally (or on paper) from the given initial state and check that after the last move the configuration matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before submitting the answer, double‑check that the move sequence achieves the target arrangement.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Provide only the move list, no extra text
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The answer should consist solely of the move list; any surrounding commentary, headings, or formatting will be ignored or cause parsing errors.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When writing the final answer, output only the list of moves.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Adding a heading like 'Solution:' before the list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, confirm that the source peg’s top disk matches the disk being moved and that the target peg’s top disk (if any) is larger.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During construction of the move sequence, after each proposed move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 when disk 2 is on top of its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear target peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never place a larger disk onto a peg that currently holds any smaller disk; first relocate those smaller disks elsewhere.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you are about to move a larger disk onto a peg that already contains disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 4 onto a peg where disk 2 is on top.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid moving small disks onto a peg that will later receive a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Do not place a small disk onto a peg if a larger disk will later need to be placed there, unless you move the small disk away before the larger arrives.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding where to temporarily store a small disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Putting disk 1 on the final target peg before moving disk 4 onto it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Move blocking smaller disks to any other peg before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is not the topmost on its source peg, first relocate all smaller disks that sit above it to another peg.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a desired larger disk is buried under smaller ones.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 4 while disk 3 remains on top of it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Smallest-disk cyclic move strategy
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Repeatedly move the smallest disk to the next peg in a fixed cyclic order (e.g., 0→1→2→0) and then make the only other legal move; this yields a correct solution for the classic Tower of Hanoi.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the puzzle starts with all disks on one peg and you need a systematic sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Breaking the cycle by moving the smallest disk to a non‑adjacent peg, causing an illegal configuration.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets to output any moves, often after focusing on reasoning.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always include at least one move; if no moves are needed, output an empty list [] explicitly.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generating before finishing the sequence, perhaps due to length limits or early termination.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After planning the full sequence, keep generating until the final move that achieves the goal is emitted.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to move a disk that is not the topmost on its source peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk based on goal order without checking the current stack.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before each move, verify that the chosen disk is the top disk on its source peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Prematurely moving a small disk onto the final target peg, causing later moves to be impossible
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model tries to place small disks early to reduce moves, overlooking that larger disks still need to be placed there.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Reserve the final target peg for larger disks until all larger disks have been moved onto it; only place the smallest disks after the larger ones are in place.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Attempted to place a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal move)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets the size ordering rule when selecting the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
